paper_metadata.title: Comparative Study of Quantum Computing Tools and Frameworks

summary: This paper is a comparative survey of quantum computing tools and frameworks, illustrating a simple 3-qubit Hadamard-based random bit generator circuit across Qiskit, QDK/Q#, Cirq, Forest/PyQuil, PennyLane-Strawberry Fields, and ProjectQ. It reports no benchmarked quantum advantage; the only quantitative hardware-related number mentioned is IBM’s 72-qubit processor capability, not an experiment result.

experiments.description: Comparative study of quantum computing tools and frameworks; includes a basic quantum random bits generator circuit demonstrated across multiple gate-based frameworks (Qiskit, QDK/Q#, Cirq, Forest/PyQuil, PennyLane-Strawberry Fields, ProjectQ).

algorithm.variant: quantum random bits generator / basic Hadamard-based circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Three qubits are placed in superposition with Hadamard gates and measured to generate random bits; no optimization problem is formulated.

problem_instance.description: Toy quantum circuit example for generating random bits and illustrating framework syntax.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Demonstration only; no quantitative benchmark protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of qubits to obtain classical random bits.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a framework comparison and toy circuit demonstration (quantum random bits generator), not a benchmarked quantum-vs-classical performance study.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No speedup benchmark or classical-vs-quantum comparison is reported; only a toy 3-qubit circuit demonstration and framework comparison are shown.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline for the circuit
No runtime, depth, or shot-based benchmark data

notes: The paper explicitly demonstrates a Hadamard-based random bit generator circuit on IBM Quantum hardware and other frameworks, but does not report a benchmarked depth, gate counts, shots, or optimization parameters.
